note: Lab clip 13, It Wasn't Resonance: the narrator only (af_heart). n05 and n06 are separate lines so the beat between them is set by hand.
ref_text: The bench outside the stall is warm from the afternoon. A kettle hisses, a cyclist rings his bell, and somebody laughs at the next table.

lines.text: Your physics book says the Tacoma Narrows Bridge fell because of resonance.
Most engineers now say it didn't.
Resonance is a push in rhythm, like pushing a swing.
That morning the wind was steady. It wasn't pushing in time with the bridge.
Its deck was shallow and solid. It caught the wind like a wing.
Each twist tipped it into the wind, and the wind pushed the twist further.
Every twist fed the next. Engineers call it flutter.
An hour later, the middle of the deck tore away.
Now big bridges are tested in a wind tunnel before they're built.
